_meta.how_to_read: Temperatures in °C. kc and stages_days follow FAO-56 (crop coefficient x reference evapotranspiration = crop water use). stages_days = [initial, development, mid-season, late-season] and sums to season_days. frost_damage_c = air temperature that damages the crop at its sensitive stage (flowering or seedling). winter_hardiness_c = lowest temperature a hardened, winter-sown crop usually survives (null for crops not sown before winter). heat_stress_c = daily maximum that harms flowering or fruit/tuber set. sensitive_das = days after sowing when the stage most sensitive to frost and heat starts (flowering; seedling for sugar beet; tuber set for potato; fruit set for tomato); it lasts about 20 days. null for perennial alfalfa. phenology (winter crops only): the calendar adapts to local temperature. Growing degree days above base_c are summed from sowing (15th of the first sowing month); the sensitive stage starts at sensitive_gdd but not before earliest_sensitive_doy (day length), and maturity comes post_gdd later. season_days, stages_days and sensitive_das are then the fallback when no temperature data is available. heat_units (warm-season crops): growing degree days between base_c and upper_c needed to reach flowering and maturity, from the FAO AquaCrop default crop files (typical varieties; local short-season varieties may need less). field_sources names the source of each imported field. temp_opt_c, temp_abs_c, soil_ph and rain_abs_mm come from FAO EcoCrop (temperatures are mean-temperature limits).

sources.FAO-56: Allen et al. 1998, FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56, Tables 11, 12 and 22 (kc, stage lengths, rooting depth)
sources.FAO EcoCrop: FAO EcoCrop database (temperature, pH and rainfall ranges)
sources.TAGEM-DSI: TAGEM-DSI crop water consumption guide for Turkey (to cross-check kc and seasons)

_meta.caveat: Values were compiled by the team from the sources above and from general agronomy references, without yet checking each value against the downloaded EcoCrop data or the TAGEM-DSI guide. Every row has verified=false until an agronomy-aware reviewer checks it.

crops.notes: Flooded (paddy) rice, irrigated only. About two thirds of Turkish rice is in Thrace-Marmara (Edirne, Balıkesir, Çanakkale) and a quarter on the Black Sea deltas (Samsun Bafra and Çarşamba, Sinop, Çorum along the Kızılırmak). Usually grown year after year; a winter vetch crop fits between rice harvests where the field drains in winter (Dok et al. 2016). Water need adds basin flooding and seepage to crop water use, because the TAGEM-DSİ guide's rice figures leave both out (its Note 2).
